texts.facts: Present petition under Section 34 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 has been filed by petitioner seeking setting aside of the Arbitral Award dated 24.11.2022, passed by Ld. Arbitrator. Brief facts of the case as set up by petitioner are that petitioner was the respondent before ld. Arbitral Tribunal. Petitioner is a firm fully covered under the provisions of MSME Act 2006. As per petition, petitioner manufactures and supplies Elastic Rail clips to the zonal railways from its unit at Bhiwadi, which was approved by Railway Development and Safety Organisation. The OMP (COMM.) No. 63/2023 (Pulastya Pramachala) District Judge (Commercial Court)-01, Page No.2 of 16 Patiala House Court, New Delhi respondent (original claimant) is the Ministry of Railways, Government of India and regularly procures ERC from the petitioner and other manufactures, for its rail network, along with other Zonal Railways. 3. Petitioner filed its bid dated 11.02.2012 offering 3,00,000 nos. of ERC with certain counter conditions in respect of price variation clause, against tender dated 20.01.2022 floated by respondent. Thereafter, petitioner at the request of respondent vide letter dated 19.04.2012 and reminder letter dated 11.05.2012, withdrew the counter conditions I the price clause of their offer and accepted the correspondent tender Price Variation Clause vide letter dated 14.06.2012. Thereafter respondent, relying on the price variation clause of the offer dated 11.02.2012, issued LOA dated 29.06.2012 and PO dated 23.07.2012, revising the offered basic rate from Rs.50.40 to Rs. 50.26 per number, giving rise to the dispute between the parties. The petitioner vide letter dated 24.11.2012 declined to accept the PO, as it was not in line with the offer of the petitioner and requested its withdrawal, but respondent refused to withdraw the PO and demanded security deposit from the petitioner. Thereafter petitioner invoked clause 2900 of the IRS condition. Meanwhile, respondent recovered security deposit amount of Rs.10.00 lakh from the petitioner's running supply bills against different PO dated 14.06.2012 and forfeited the same. Ld. arbitrator was appointed. Respondent had filed a Statement of Claim, which was subsequently withdrawn. Petitioner filed Statement of Defence with Counter Claim. Ld. arbitrator however, disallowed the counter claim no. B and C. GROUNDS OF OBJECTION/CHALLENGE 4. Aggrieved by the Arbitral Award dated 24.11.2022, petitioner has filed present objections under Section 34 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, mainly on the following grounds: - M/S Simtech International vs Union Of India on 7 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62235821/ 2 i. Because the award is in conflict with the public policy and is vitiated by patent illegality and is not sustainable in the eyes of law; ii. Because ld. arbitrator disallowed the counter claim no. B and C. iii. Because ld. arbitrator held that GCC does not allow payment of interest on earnest money, security deposit and performance guarantee. iv. Because ld. arbitrator despite holding that the contract was void and recovery of Rs.10.00 lakh was bad in law, disallowed the counter claim no. B. v. Because ld. arbitrator with respect to counter claim no. C, held that contract/agreement between the parties was silent as to the liability towards payment of the fee and expenses incurred during the arbitral proceedings. vi. Because ld. arbitrator failed to appreciate the fact that the petitioner had incurred huge expense during this period of almost 10 years in litigating the disputes. REPLY FILED BY RESPONDENT 5. Respondent filed a reply contesting the present petition. It is contended that the petitioner is suppressing the material facts and OMP (COMM.) No. 63/2023 (Pulastya Pramachala) District Judge (Commercial Court)-01, Page No.4 of 16 Patiala House Court, New Delhi has not come with clean hands. Respondent submitted that payment of Rs.10.00 lakh has been made to the petitioner. Respondent submitted that petitioner has accepted the arbitration award and filed application before Rajasthan Micro and Small Enterprises Facilitation Council for the refund of Rs.10.00 lakhs and interest, which is unlawful because these claims were already under adjudication as per arbitration clause, which was revoked by the petitioner on 26.02.2013. Respondent averred that averments in the objection petition does not satisfy any cause of action in favour of petitioner.
texts.arguments: On merits, respondent denied the averments made in the petition and stated that contract was governed by clause 2401 of IRS conditions, which clearly stipulates that: - "Whenever any claim or claims for payment of a sum of money arises out of or under the contract against the Contractor, the Purchaser shall be entitled to withhold and also have a lien to retain such sum or sums in whole or in part from the security, if any, deposited by the Contractor and for the purpose aforesaid, the Purchaser shall be entitled to withhold the said cash security deposit or the security, if any, furnished as the case may be and also have a lien over the same pending finalization or adjudication of any such claim. In the event of the security being insufficient to cover the claimed amount or amounts or if no security has been taken from the Contractor, the Purchaser shall be entitled to withhold and have lien to retain to the extent of the such claimed amount or amounts referred to supra, from any sum or sums found payable or which at any time thereafter may become payable to the Contractor under the same contract or any other contract with the Purchaser or the Government pending finalization or adjudication of any such claim. Hence it can be ascertained from this clause that Ld. Sole arbitrator rightly dismissed the counter claim no. B by pronouncing award as per terms and conditions of the contract. Ld. counsel for petitioner argued that ld. arbitrator could not have relied upon GCC conditions to disallow counter claim no. B, when he himself held that PO dated 23.07.2012 was void. Ld. counsel averred that conditions in agreement/contract and GCC, if applicable, would apply only if there was a valid contract between parties. Ld. counsel argued that reliance of respondent to IRS conditions, is erroneous as the contract itself was held void by ld. arbitrator. Petitioner further averred that ld. arbitrator could not have relied on contract to disallow counter claim no. C, since petitioner incurred huge expense during this period of almost 10 years in litigating the disputes with the respondent. Ld. counsel relying on Section 24 of MSME Act, argued that MSME Act has an overriding effect, the petitioner is entitled to interest as per MSME Act. 7. Ld. counsel for the petitioner argued that MSME Act prevails over contract/PO dated 23.07.2012 and as such reliance on GCC clauses or IRS Conditions are misplaced. Ld. counsel further argued that now it is settled that courts have discretionary power under Section 34/37 of the Act to modify the award in question. Ld. counsel further averred that ld. arbitrator could not have relied on the contract and he should have granted interest under MSME Act. Respondent argued that the payment of Rs. 10,00,000/- has since been made by the respondent to the petitioner in compliance with the award rendered by the Ld. Sole Arbitrator. It was argued that arbitrator has rightly and justifiably rejected the counter claim nos. B and C of the petitioner, supported by detailed and well-reasoned grounds for their rejection. Ld. counsel argued that even assuming for the sake argument, without admitting, the P.O/Contract was declared void, such declaration does not affect the applicability of IRS or GCC, as participation in the tender process itself establishes a binding legal relationship/contractual framework governed by these terms.
